newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sells 80 pct stake in Banco Popular.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sells 80 pct stake in Banco Popular.

text.p: Colombia sold an 80 percent stake in state-run Banco Popular, the country's seventh largest bank in terms of assets, for 271.9 billion pesos, a spokesman for Bogota's stock exchange said.

The identity of the buyer was not immediately known but the an offshore holding company controlled by Luis Carlos Sarmiento Angulo, one of Colombia's wealthiest entrepreneurs, was the only qualified bidder for the bank, according to Carlos Caballero, chairman of the Bogota exchange.

The privatization was the biggest in Colombia this year. In the nine-months to September, Banco Popular posted net profits of 20.31 billion pesos, up 133 percent compared to the same period in 1995. Its total assets to September this year stood at 1.5 trillion pesos.
The 80 percent stake, consisting of 4.48 billion 60.6 peso shares, in Banco Popular was conducted simultaneously through the bourses in Bogota, Medellin and Cali.

Sarmiento already controls Banco de Bogota, Colombia's fourth largest bank in terms of assets and Banco Occidente, the ninth largest bank, and has other interests in savings banks, building societies and financial corporations.
